learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the chemical balancing process.
Knowledge of the chemical-structural characteristics of matter.
Ability to derive the electronic configuration of an element and predict its reactivity.
Ability to calculate the heat exchanged following a chemical transformation of the system.
Ability to predict whether a transformation is spontaneous or not.
Autonomy of judgment: ability to compare different solutions and determine the most appropriate.
Learning ability: autonomous study for the application of studied models to new chemical problems.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION: Definition of matter. Elements and compounds. Atomic theory of matter. Fundamental laws of chemistry: consequences.

ATOM, MOLECULE, MOLE. MINIMUM AND MOLECULAR FORMULA: Atomic and mass number. Isotopes. Mass defect. Atomic mass and molecular mass. Avogadro's number and concept of mole. Molar mass. Weight percentage of elements in a compound.

THE ELECTRICAL NATURE OF MATTER AND ATOMIC STRUCTURE: Brief history of the evolution of atomic theory. Radioactivity. Thomson's experiment. Rutherford's experiment. The planetary model of the atom. Emission and absorption spectra. Rydberg equation. Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom. Insufficiency of the Bohr model. Sommerfeld and Zeeman theories. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle. De Broglie hypothesis. Schrödinger equation. Wave function " and its probabilistic meaning. Atomic orbitals. Multi-electron atoms. The spin quantum number. Aufbau principles: Pauli's principle and Hund's rule.
ELECTRONIC CONFIGURATION OF ELEMENTS AND PERIODIC TABLE: Electronic configuration. The periodic table. Periodic properties of elements.

CHEMICAL BONDING: Ionic bond, lattice energy. Covalent bond. Valence Bond theory and diatomic and polyatomic molecules and ions. VSEPR theory. Hybridization sp, sp2, sp3, sp3d, sp3d2. Concept of resonance, electroneutrality principle. Electrical and magnetic characteristics of molecules.
CHEMICAL NOMENCLATURE: Oxidation number. Chemical nomenclature of binary compounds, oxyacids, salts and complexes.
CHEMICAL REACTIONS: Acid-base and redox reactions. Balancing reactions. Stoichiometric calculations and limiting reagent.

GAS LAWS: States of aggregation of matter: solids, liquids and gases. Ideal gas equation of state. Isothermal transformations (Boyle's law), isobaric transformations (Charles's law) and isochoric transformations (Gay-Lussac's law). Gas density. Ideal gases in chemical reactions.
SOLUTIONS AND REACTIONS IN SOLUTION: Solutions. Ways of expressing concentrations. Volumetric ratios in chemical reactions.

THERMODYNAMICS: System and state variables, heat and work, zero principle and definition of temperature. State functions. Internal energy. First principle. Specific heat. Definition of standard state. Enthalpy. Hess's law.
assessment_rules: The assessment includes an oral exam, potentially preceded by a written test. Minimum requirements for passing are knowledge of the periodic table, chemical bonding, matter and energy (heat) balance of a chemical reaction, and the ability to set up and solve stoichiometry problems. Grading ranges from Excellent (30-30 cum laude) for excellent knowledge and analytical ability to Insufficient if acceptable knowledge of the program content is not demonstrated.
